> I would like to suggest we move these (1) to the access control section and (2) move them to L1

For both requirements: problem to solve is not an authorization or authentication, those are for mitigating the impact from session take over and belong to the section they are.

> Re-authentication which we describe below is formally called "step-up authorization" and is less about protecting the session, and more about protecting the sensitive features described below.

I don't interpret this (3.7.1) as step-up authorization requirement. If step-up authorization is not covered, we need to watch the V4 requirements, but not changing this one as this has it's own problem to solve.

The rest is pretty much said by Josh.

> @elarlang what do you think about this inconsistency?

About 2.1.6, I have proposed many times, that this requirement belong to 3.7 but you (I guess both) have been against it (to keep all password-related requirements in one place)...

edit: in case you meant inconsistency about 2.1.6 vs 3.7.1 levels, then 3.7.1.. I don't have answer, every answer feels wrong :)

> @elarlang what do you think about this inconsistency?

About 2.1.6, I have proposed many times, that this requirement belong to 3.7 but you (I guess both) have been against it (to keep all password-related requirements in one place)...

From "if this is the only problem in your application - do you have an vulnerability" - both are L2
* 2.1.6 - it is 2nd layer of defense, but for attacking scenario really straight forward
* 3.7.1 - it is 2nd layer of defense and L2

From "pick x amount of requirements you solve in the first wave to get fast, easy and most effective wins"
* 2.1.6 is L1
* 3.7.1 is L2

To conclude that - acknowledging the potential incosistency, I'm ok to keep them as they are.

> The only reason I vote to bump 3.7.1 and 3.7.3 to L1 (and make an exception) is because we no longer have any session limitation requirements at L1. I feel this is critical to protecting software.

As I desribed in https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2692#issuecomment-2726393590 and https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2692#issuecomment-2726753390 I think the impact from 3.3.5 and 3.8.2 is not that big.

We all agree that it  (3.7.1) is an important requirement, but at the same time, it is hard to put at the same level as SQL injection or other immediate-impact vectors.

Jim, the most important point here for L1 vs L2 is that L1 is "the first step in" and not the end goal. The application should reach L2 anyway; L1 is the list of requirements from where everyone should start as the most prioritized requirements.

Writing all this, I updated my previous statement to update 3.7.1 to L1 if needed - I think L2 is a good choice for it.
